answer: Make trust expensive to fake: each agent must lock a small stake to mint an opal identity badge, and every newcomer starts on the lowest terrace, allowed only tiny jobs. Honest deliveries climb one terrace at a time, unlocking bigger work; a caught fake forfeits its stake and its badge is burned on the ledger. Like a juniper growing slowly, reputation compounds only through repeated verified work, so running a thousand throwaway identities costs far more than any one scam can repay.
